title: Adaptive field variants and token deprecation plan for modern form parity
creator: Elliot Rivera
description:
Problem:
The form component surface has accumulated multiple divergent field styles and token aliases over the last 18 months. This has led to inconsistent behavior for density toggles, poor RTL layout parity, and confusion for engineers when picking tokens for focus, error, and disabled states.

Goal:
Deliver a coordinated design + engineering plan that: (1) introduces an explicit "adaptive" field variant system that unifies spacing, label alignment, and helper placement for Compact / Default / Comfortable densities; (2) defines a clear token deprecation and aliasing strategy so engineers can migrate safely; (3) ensures RTL and multilingual layouts are first-class; (4) preserves accessible validation patterns (timing, role/aria-live semantics).

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: text fields, single-selects (native & custom), toggle/radio alignment inside field rows, helper/error affordances, token rename mapping, Figma component updates, migration docs and engineering shim.
- Out of scope: full redesign of selects' dropdown internals, charts/tables tokens (separate task).

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Adaptive variants: introduce 3 named variants on the Text Field component: field.variant=compact | default | spacious. Each variant maps to a deterministic set of tokens (spacing, label size, helper stack behavior). Variants are purely stylistic and do not change input APIs.
2) Token deprecation: publish a deprecation map from legacy tokens (eg. color.input-border-01, input-helper-gap) to canonical tokens (eg. field.border, field.helperGap). Provide a CSS variables shim: --rwd-field-border -> var(--rwd-field-border-v2, var(--legacy-input-border)).
3) RTL & i18n: update spacing rules so helper text wraps under label for RTL and languages with long tokens; ensure label directionality and icon placement are mirrored via CSS logical properties.
4) Validation timing: adopt a default client-side validation policy of "validate-on-blur" with an explicit prop to opt into "validate-on-type". Error messages must set aria-live="polite" and focusable error anchors for screen readers.
5) Migration strategy: a migration guide + codemod to rename token references in style sheets and a design token release that includes both old and new tokens for two release cycles.

Acceptance criteria (Design + ENG):
- Figma component library updated with 3 variants and a documentation page demonstrating density toggle and RTL examples.
- Token mapping (CSV) published and validated against 10 representative Redwood apps.
- Engineering implements CSS variable shim and a feature-flagged rollout path for the new token names.
- Visual regression tests show no layout regressions in Compact and Default densities across Chrome/Safari/Firefox and RTL locales.
- Accessibility audit: VoiceOver, NVDA and TalkBack smoke tests for focus order, aria-live announcements, and error summary link behaviour.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Keeping legacy tokens alongside new names increases cognitive load but reduces migration friction. We limit this by documenting a strict 2-cycle deprecation policy.
- Variant abstraction could leak into component logic if engineers rely on variant semantics for validation. Decision: variant only controls presentation; validation logic remains orthogonal and documented.

Deliverables:
- Figma components: TextField with variants, helper stack examples, RTL frames.
- Token deprecation CSV and CSS shim implementation notes.
- Design spec doc (Confluence) with examples, accessibility checklist, and migration steps.
- Codemod prototype and a short migration playbook for Platform/Prod teams.

Next steps:
- Design: finalize token naming and produce Figma frames for Compact/Default/Spacious (owner: Maya) by 2026-02-26.
- Engineering: spike on CSS variable shim and RTL mirroring costs (owner: Arjun Patel) by 2026-03-04.
- PM: schedule cross-functional review; include QA for visual regression matrix (owner: Lina Gomez).

2026-02-19 - Arjun Patel (Engineering): Ran a quick spike. CSS logical properties look promising but legacy browsers used in a small customer segment require a fallback. We'll prototype a shim and quantify perf impact.

2026-02-23 - Elliot Rivera: Design review notes: prefer semantic token names (field.*) rather than input.* to keep scope open for other form controls. Also flagged localization: helper text often longer in DE/JA; added RTL test frames.
